findings.description: The security group permits TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the instance.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the instance.

Static AWS access key and secret key are embedded in the EC2 user_data script; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances or from the instance metadata service, leaking long-lived credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the instance allows IMDSv1 unauthenticated metadata requests, turning any SSRF in the web application into credential theft.

The instance has no root_block_device encryption specified and is launched into a public subnet with an auto-assigned public IP, placing the host directly on the internet with unencrypted root storage.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so data stored on the attached disk is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot inherits the unencrypted source volume, so backup data is stored without encryption and could be shared or restored without key controls.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration or KMS key), so sensitive network audit logs are stored unencrypted.
No public access block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, risking public or cross-account exposure of network telemetry.

The log bucket lacks versioning and a policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport, so audit logs can be overwritten/deleted irrecoverably and may be transmitted without encryption in transit. force_destroy = true further allows silent deletion of audit data.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, placing workloads directly on the internet rather than in a private network layer.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically exposes all instances in this subnet with public IP addresses, contrary to placing components without inbound internet requirements in private subnets.
The VPC's default security group is never explicitly restricted via aws_default_security_group, so it retains permissive intra-group allow rules that were not authored or reviewed.
